about: The offertory antiphon of the First Sunday of Advent, Psalm 24:1–3 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 25 in Hebrew). The typical edition prints here, word for word, the verses the introit sang.

seg.tr: To You I lift up my soul. O my God, in You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

a.g: let me not be put to shame

ex.w013: The psalmist asks that his trust in God not be disappointed. The Hebrew volitive form and Greek optative also support reading these words as a plea.

nt.w013: “Erubéscam” can express a plea, “let me not be put to shame,” or a future statement, “I shall not be put to shame.” The Latin ending itself is shared by both readings.
